findings.title: remove() invalidates login cache using post-removal lookup of storedIdp which may not reflect prior login eligibility correctly
findings.body: In remove(), storedIdp is fetched from idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) before removal, which is correct, but registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) is called with storedIdp possibly null if the alias doesn't exist. getLoginPredicate().test(idp) does handle null via Objects::nonNull check, so this is safe, but note that in the invalid branch (isInvalid(cacheKey)), registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) is also called with potentially null storedIdp passed into registerIDPInvalidation which calls idp.getInternalId() without a null check, causing a NullPointerException if the alias does not match any identity provider.

findings.title: getForLogin cache keyed only by FetchMode, not by organizationId, except via per-searchKey entries growing unbounded
findings.body: The IdentityProviderListQuery cached under cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode) accumulates entries per distinct organizationId searchKey (ORG_ONLY/ALL modes). Since organizationId can vary per request/organization, this list query cache can grow without bound as more organizations are queried over the realm's lifetime, with no eviction of stale per-org entries other than full invalidation. This differs from the by-organization cache which is keyed per org (cacheKeyOrgId), bounding growth to one entry per org; here all orgs share one IdentityProviderListQuery object which may grow large for realms with many organizations, impacting cache memory and lookup cost.

findings.title: create() invalidates login cache using the model before internalId/alias is set by delegate
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidation(model) is called before idpDelegate.create(model), using the model as passed in which may not yet have config fully normalized (e.g., defaults applied) by the delegate. If getLoginPredicate() depends on fields normalized during creation (e.g., default enabled/hideOnLogin values applied by the delegate), the invalidation decision could be based on stale/incomplete data, potentially causing newly created login-eligible IDPs to not invalidate the cache so stale results are served until next change.
